items.title: Joey Morant interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013
items.q: I did that with Harold Cutlett in Ontario, many times. I put a handkerchief over the phone back then... I got me work like that.

ctx.x: What’s it been like to make a living as a musician?

Good for me. I never experienced a real downside. I had times when I didn’t work. It didn’t bother me. Because the psychology in my nature took me to another job. I made the right phone calls to the right agent at the right time, impressed him in the right manner to get the right job. Hallelujah. Another musician may be a hell of a player but can’t do that. I used to call guys and pretend I was my agent. “I have this trumpet player, he’s very good, he’s a great guy, he happens to be black and he needs a job right…
Is it hard to find musicians —
